name: Da Fu
description: Da Fu is a traditional Chinese money-card game played in the same money-suited ecosystem as Quan Dui and Luk Fu, emphasizing pair and sequence construction under draw-discard flow.

overview.description: Da Fu is a traditional Chinese money-card game played in the same money-suited ecosystem as Quan Dui and Luk Fu, emphasizing pair and sequence construction under draw-discard flow.

history.origins: Dates back to the Qing Dynasty. Money cards (divided into Coins, Strings, and Myriads) were the direct ancestors of modern Mahjong tiles. Quan Dui evolved as a faster, pair-focused variant of the more complex 'Guan Pai' games.
timeline: 1800s: Widespread in tea houses and gambling dens of Guangdong.
1920s: Rules for 'Ka' and 'Dui' differentiate into its modern form.
1980s: Standardized for casual play in Hong Kong and Southern China.
Present: Still played by elders and cultural enthusiasts using traditional narrow cards.
history.cultural: Often played with narrow, long cards that are held in a unique 'Fan' shape characteristic of Chinese card traditions.
history.evolution: The game shifted from a purely numerical matching game into a 'Dui-Priority' game where the physical identity of the cards (exact suit/rank match) became the most valuable mechanic.

setup.deck: 120 cards (3 suits: Coins, Strings, Myriads; 4 sets of 1-9 each; plus 3 Special cards).
setup.dealing: Dealer gets 16 cards, others get 15. Counter-clockwise play.

rules.objective: The object is to collect a 16-card hand consisting of eight pairs (dui or ka). The first player to do so exposes their cards and wins the agreed stake from each opponent; if all eight pairs are identical (dui), the winner collects double stake (quan dui).
rules.gameplay: Play is anticlockwise. The dealer begins by discarding one card face up. Only the most recently discarded card may be taken. Priority to take the discard: (1) any player who can complete eight pairs and win; (2) any player who can form a Dui (identical pair) with the discard; (3) the player to the right of the discarder, who may take it if no one else does. If you take the discard to form a Dui, place the pair face up in front of you and discard one card; the player to your right plays next. If no one takes the discard, the next player in turn may either take the discard or draw the top card from the stock, then discards one card face up. Play continues until someone has eight pairs and wins.
keyRules: Dui is a pair of identical cards; Ka is a pair of same number in different suits. The three odd cards count as ones. Completing eight pairs wins; all eight Dui (quan dui) pays double stake. Winner may optionally continue playing for quan dui instead of claiming with mixed Ka and Dui, unless the final pair was claimed from the discard as Ka.

strategy.basic: Prioritize your 'Dui' (True Pairs). Because they give you priority to jump the turn order, having two identical cards in hand is a major defensive move—you can 'Steal' the turn from your opponents at any time. Avoid holding 'Ka' (False Pairs) if you can, as they are easily blocked by players holding the matching Dui cards.
strategy.intermediate: Hand Thinning: Focus your collection on one or two suits. Since there are only 4 of each card in the 120-card deck, if you hold two identical 5-Strings, the probability of someone else having the other two is manageable. If you spread across all three suits, you are less likely to stumble upon the specific cards needed for a Dui.
strategy.advanced: Discard Baiting: If you have a 'Dui' of 4-Coins and a singleton 5-Coins, discard the 5. This signals to opponents that you aren't interested in that range, potentially inducing them to discard their 4-Coins later in the round. This 'Social Engineering' of the discard pile is common among veteran Quan Dui gamblers.
tips: Watch the 'Special' cards (Xiao Hong, Ba Shu). They only form Ka pairs and are worth fewer points in 'Double Payout' house rules.
If the stockpile is low, switch to purely defensive play to force a draw.

variations.name: Quan Dui double stake
variations.description: When the winner has all eight pairs as Dui (identical cards), they collect double the agreed stake from each opponent.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes stake multiplier; no engine overrides needed.

variations.name: Optional win claim
variations.description: With eight pairs of mixed Ka and Dui, the player may choose to continue playing for quan dui instead of claiming; if the final pair was claimed from the discard as Ka, they must expose and win single stake.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only affects optional claim timing; no engine overrides needed.

scoring.description: Winner collects agreed stake from each other player; if all eight pairs are Dui (quan dui), double stake is collected.
scoring.winCondition: First player to form eight pairs (16 cards) wins the hand. Expose your hand and collect one stake per opponent; if all eight pairs are identical-card Dui, collect double stake (quan dui).
